Toronto neighbourhoods, mapped onto San Francisco

Both maps drawn at the same scale from OpenStreetMap data, so the size comparison is honest
The six numbered pins are my primary matches; the hollow pins are the alternates I mentioned. The striking thing once it's on a map: SF packs all six equivalents into a noticeably tighter footprint than Toronto's spread — but stacks several hundred metres of climbing into that smaller space.

San Francisco

Solid numbered pins = primary match. Hollow pins = alternate candidate. Basemap © OpenStreetMap contributors.

The pairings

TorontoSan FranciscoThe shared quality
Rosedale1Pacific Heights (c: 75%)Old money, grand houses, quiet streets, walkable to downtown
High Park-Swansea2Inner Sunset (c: 70%)Leafy family residential wrapped around a huge park — Golden Gate Park plays the High Park role almost exactly
Roncesvalles3Noe Valley (c: 60%)Gentrified main-street strip, indie shops, stroller density
Danforth / Greektown4Inner Richmond (c: 65%)A long, still-working immigrant commercial spine (Clement St). North Beach is the tourist-facing version
Leslieville5Bernal Heights (c: 60%)Ex-working-class, now young families and brunch, with Cortland Ave as its Queen St E
The Beaches6Outer Sunset (c: 60%)Beach-town-inside-a-city, relaxed. Though The Beaches is far more affluent — that side is closer to Marina/Cow Hollow

Pins sit on each neighbourhood's geocoded centroid, so they mark the area's rough middle rather than its high street.

Toronto — your actual route, same scale

The red line is the real road-following cycling route (21.6 km), not a straight-line sketch. Basemap © OpenStreetMap contributors.

What the maps show that the list didn't

Compactness. Your Toronto loop stretches about 10 km end to end. The SF equivalents span roughly 10 km too, but on a diagonal across a peninsula rather than strung along a lakeshore — so an SF version would double back on itself far more.

Hills. The Toronto route is essentially flat. An SF equivalent linking Pacific Heights, Noe Valley, Bernal Heights and Outer Sunset would involve several hundred metres of cumulative climbing (c: 70%) — shorter in distance, likely longer in elapsed time and much harder work.

The park anchors line up neatly. Golden Gate Park sits between Inner Sunset and Outer Sunset the same way High Park sits beside Swansea — that pairing is the most structurally exact of the six.
